findings.issue: Wrong reading of 気に入って: the idiom 気に入る is read きにいる (kiniiru), never きにはいる. The kana transcribes it as きにはいって.
findings.current: これわちちにきにはいってもらう。
findings.suggested: これわちちにきにいってもらう。

findings.issue: Token 入っ inside 気に入って must be read いっ (from 気に入る = きにいる), not はいっ. Reading はいっ teaches the wrong pronunciation of this fixed expression.
Romaji propagates the wrong reading of 気に入って: 'kinihaitte' should be 'kiniitte' (kiniiru idiom).
パターン means 'pattern' in this sentence (and generally); 'standard' is a wrong sense, apparently back-translated from pt 'padrão'. The sentence-level en itself says 'pattern'.

The parenthetical claims the sentence uses the 〜でいっぱい pattern, but there is no で here; 〜でいっぱい means 'full OF X' with で marking the filler. This is simply predicative いっぱい + です and the wrong pattern label can mislead learners.
findings.current: いっぱい appears as a predicate with the sense of 'full/packed' (the 〜でいっぱい pattern in stative use), closed by です.
findings.suggested: いっぱい appears as a predicate with the sense of 'full/packed' (predicative use of いっぱい), closed by です.

findings.issue: Same wrong pattern attribution as expl_en: cites 'padrão 〜でいっぱい' although the sentence contains no で; it is plain predicative いっぱい + です.
findings.current: いっぱい aparece como predicado com o sentido de 'cheio/lotado' (padrão 〜でいっぱい no uso de estado), fechado por です.
findings.suggested: いっぱい aparece como predicado com o sentido de 'cheio/lotado' (uso predicativo de いっぱい), fechado por です.

findings.issue: Literal rendering is inaccurate: はずだ expresses logical expectation ('it is to be expected'), not 'of course'; the stray '(standard)' gloss is also the wrong sense of パターン. lit_pt got it right ('é de se esperar').
findings.suggested: There's a pattern, it is to be expected.

findings.issue: Adds a demonstrative not present in the Japanese: ホテルには has no この, so the literal mirror should say 'the hotel' (lit_pt correctly has 'Quanto ao hotel').
findings.current: As for this hotel, foreigners are many.
findings.suggested: As for the hotel, foreigners are many.
